findings.title: Index on a ~400M-row table is not created CONCURRENTLY
findings.explanation: docs/CONVENTIONS.md says indexes on `events`, which has about 400 million rows, must use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`. A plain `CREATE INDEX` takes a SHARE lock on the table for the whole build. That blocks every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on `events`, so event writes would stall for the duration of the build, which could be minutes to hours on a table this size. Change the statement to `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_project_id_idx ON events (project_id, id DESC);`.

findings.title: Missing `-- migrate:no-transaction` header
findings.explanation: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` cannot run inside a transaction block, and the migration runner wraps migrations in one by default. The convention, and `004_events.sql`, put `-- migrate:no-transaction` on the first line of the file. Without it, the concurrent build fails once the first fix is applied. Add the header as line 1.

findings.title: Make the migration safe to re-run after a failed concurrent build
findings.explanation: A failed `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` leaves an INVALID index behind under the same name. A retry then fails with 'relation already exists'. Consider `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS`, and add a note in the PR on how to check for and drop an invalid index (`DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_project_id_idx`) before retrying.

findings.title: Index is correct for the query; consider noting the NULL project_id rows
findings.explanation: The index (project_id, id DESC) matches `WHERE project_id = $1 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 100` in src/routes/projects.ts, so the index choice itself is fine. `project_id` is nullable, and many events probably have no project. Those rows would bloat the index. A partial index with `WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL` would be smaller. Optional. It would also be useful to put EXPLAIN output or timing numbers in the PR description to back up the speed-up claim.
